newsitem.title: USA: Drifting U.S. sour crude prices return to level.
newsitem.headline: Drifting U.S. sour crude prices return to level.

text.p: Cash crude prices in the U.S. Gulf extended a mostly steady session for domestic grade differentials to Monday afternoon, though sour barrels saw earlier advances retreat after refiner buying dissipated.
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing floated around 20 cents lower at $19.85-19.95 a barrel, with September/October spreads at minus 23 cents.

Traders in the Gulf said a number of large refiners came in the sour market this morning and covered needs that had accumulated in recent days. The drive for supply lifted West Texas Sour/Midland to a $1.10 discount under WTI/Cushing, 20-25 cents stronger than last deals on Friday.
"People saw there were only four days left (for September domestic trade), and they were behind in their needs," said a trader in Houston.
Since the morning, however, WTS price differentials have retreated to discounts of $1.20-25 under WTI, more closely resembling the performance of late last week.
On the sweet side of the market, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James talked at 23-25 cents over marker, steady from Friday. WTI/Cushing Postings Plus was at $1.83-85, down a few cents.
